8243.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MA1003 : Mathematics - I { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1 (16 hours)
Differential Calculus: Real number system, Completeness axiom, Sequences (monotone, bounded, Cauchy) and their convergence Series of real numbers, Tests for convergence of Series Limit, Continuity and Differentiability of functions of one variable, Rolle’s Theorem, Mean value theorems, Limit, Continuity and Differentiability of functions of several variables, Partial Differentiation, Total Differentiation, Change of Variables – Jacobians.
Module 2 (10 hours)
Integral Calculus: Riemann integration, Introduction to improper integrals, Beta and Gamma integrals, Differentiation under the integral sign Double and triple integrals.
Module 3 (10 hours)
Vector Calculus: Scalar and Vector fields, Vector differentiation, Gradient of scalar field, Directional derivative, Divergence and Curl of a vector field, Laplacian operator. Line, surface, and volume integrals, Green’s theorem in the plane, Gauss divergence theorem, and Stokes’s theorem.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce the properties of real numbers and give an idea of proofs in real analysis.
2 .

To understand the concepts involved in limit via the epsilon method (for sequences as well as for functions of one/several variables).
3 .

To introduce the idea behind Riemann integration through upper/lower Riemann sums.
4 .

To introduce the concepts of vector differentiation and integration.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Students will learn about different types of sequences, series, and results related to their convergence.
CO2: Students will learn the epsilon-delta approach for limit, continuity, and differentiability along with the difference between the differential functions of one variable and several variables.
CO3: Students will learn about the applications of basic theorems on continuity and differentiability, and the method of determining maxima/minima of functions of several variables.
CO4: Students will be able to test the Riemann integrability of elementary functions, calculate double/triple integrals change the order of integration, and test the convergence of improper integrals.
CO5: They will learn about differential operators and vector integration, their properties, and applications.

Essential Reading

1 .

Maurice D. Weir, Joel Hass & Christopher Heil, Thomas’ Calculus Early Transcendentals, Thirteenth Edition, Pearson Education, Inc.

2 .

T. M. Apostol, Calculus, Volume I and II, John Wiley & Sons, Inc.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Robert G. Bartle & Donald R. Sherbert, Introduction to Real Analysis, John Wiley & Sons, Inc.

2 .

ERWIN KREYSZIG, ADVANCED ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS, John Wiley & Sons, Inc.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC6601 : Advanced Digital Signal Processing { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1:LTI Discrete-Time Systems in the Transform Domain: Transfer function classification based on magnitude and phase characteristics, Types of Linear-phase FIR transfer functions, simple digital filters, Complementary transfer functions, Inverse systems, Algebraic stability test. [4Hours]
Module 2:Digital filter structures: Basic FIR and IIR filter structures, Allpass filters, Computational complexity of digital filter structures. [6 Hours]
Module 3:IIR digital filter design: Design of lowpass, highpass, bandpass and bandstop IIR filters, Spectral transformations, Computer-aided design of IIR digital filter FIR digital filter design: Design based on windowed Fourier series, Computer-aided design of FIR digital filter, Design of computationally efficient FIR digital filters. [8 Hours]
Module 4: Multirate DSP: Interpolation and decimation filter bank design polyphasestructures. [10 Hours]
Module 5: Adaptive systems: Examples and applications. Adaptive linear combiner: the performance function, gradient and minimum mean square error, alternative expression of gradient, LMS, complex LMS, NLMS, sign-error, transform domain LMS, Recursive least square algorithm, windowed RLS, computational complexity, Block adaptive filter, Convergence analysis. [10 Hours]

Course Objective

1 .

To provide detailed understanding of digital filter design and stability analysis.
2 .

Learning about designing adaptive systems for filtering applications.
3 .

Understanding of multirate systems and their applications for signal analysis and synthesis.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1:Students will learn how to design an application specific filter for the given specifications.
CO2: Understanding of digital filter structures to lessen the overall computational cost of the system.
CO3: Utility of multirate systems and their applications in signal analysis.
CO4: Thoughtful of adaptive systems and their utility in real-time processing of signals.
CO5: Student will learn different types of adaptive filters and subsequently use them based on the requirements.

Subject Nature : Practical

6. Generation of a PAM signal using MATLAB, and its analysis for different sampling frequencies in time and frequency domain.

Implementation of Analog and Digital modulation schemes using trainer kits.

Implementation of Analog and Digital modulation schemes using MATLAB.
3 .

Comparison of different modulation techniques.

Analysis of modulated signals in time and frequency domain.

After the completion of this course, students will be able to:

(BL1 and BL2)

(BL3 and BL4)

(BL3 and BL4)

(BL3 and BL4)

(BL3 and BL4)

8755.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA4468 : ECBC and Eco-Niwas Compliance { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I- Compliance and Approach:
Energy Performance Index (EPI), Determining EPI Ratio, EPI ratio for core and shell buildings, EPI ratio for mixed-use development, prescriptive method, whole building performance method, new building compliance, additions and alterations to existing buildings, approved compliance tools, compliance documents.
Assignment(s): Describing the basic requirements as per ECBC, 2007
Module II- Building Envelope:
Fenestration, opaque construction, daylighting, building envelope sealing, roof, opaque external wall, vertical fenestration, skylights, building envelope trade-off method
Assignment(s): Describing the building envelope design for a commercial building
Module III- Comfort Systems and Controls:
Ventilation, minimum space conditioning equipment efficiencies, controls, piping and ductwork, system balancing, condensers, service water heating, chillers, pumps, cooling towers, boilers, economizers, variable flow hydronic systems, unitary, split, packaged air-conditioners, controls for ECBC+ and Super ECBC buildings, controls for super ECBC buildings, energy recovery, service water heating, total system efficiency – alternate compliance approach, low-energy comfort systems
Assignment(s): Describing the comfort systems and controls for a commercial building
Module IV- Lighting and Controls:
Lighting control, exit signs, interior lighting power, building area method, space function method, installed interior lighting power, exterior lighting power, controls for ECBC+ and Super ECBC buildings.
Assignment(s): Describing the lighting controls for a commercial building
Module V- ECONIWAS Samhita 2018- Building Envelope:
Terminology and definitions, climatic zone and classification of cities, calculation of openable window-to-floor area ratio (WFRop), calculation of window-to-wall ratio (WWR), calculation of thermal transmittance (U-value) of roof and wall, orientation factor, calculation of equivalent SHGC, guidelines for design for natural ventilation, cool roof, and roof Gardens.
Assignment(s): Describing the important aspects of Eco-Niwas Samhita, 2018
Module VI- ECONIWAS 2.0 – Basic Tool:
Selecting project location, defining shading, area, and orientation, defining building envelope (wall, roof, and window), Air-conditioning and Ventilation techniques, selecting energy efficient parameters in building design.
Assignment(s): Performing energy demand simulation for a small-sized residential building using basic tools
Module VII- ECONIWAS 2.0 – Advanced Tool:
Basic information level, geometry information level, envelope information level, construction details level, dimensional details level, lighting information level, defining lighting load using building area method, defining lighting load using space function method, equipment information level, defining equipment load using building area method, defining equipment load using space function method, HVAC information level, results panel, performance comparison.
Assignment(s): Performing energy demand simulation for a small-sized residential building using advanced tools
Module VIII- ECONIWAS 2.0 – Envelope Optimization Tool:
Selecting the choice of base wall/roof assembly on which insulation of optimized thickness shall be installed, selection of insulation material, selection of window type based on corresponding cost, selecting window-to-wall ratio (WWR) of each façade, optimizing U-value, SHGC for envelope components.
Assignment(s): Performing energy demand simulation for a small-sized residential building using envelope optimization tools

Course Objective

1 .

To develop an understanding of designing a commercial building complied with the Energy Conservation Building Code of India (ECBC), 2007.
2 .

To acquire knowledge of minimum performance standards for building envelope, limiting heat gains/loss, and achieving adequate natural ventilation and daylight for a new residential building as specified in Eco-Niwas Samhita, 2018.
3 .

To understand the code compliance and to provide the minimum requirement(s) for building services, electro-mechanical, and renewable energy systems for new residential buildings.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to design a new commercial building complied with the ECBC, 2007.
2. Ability to use energy simulation tools applicable to a commercial building.
3. Ability to design a new residential building complied with the Eco-Niwas Samhita, 2018.
4. Ability to use energy simulation tools applicable to a residential building.

Essential Reading

Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Energy Conservation Building Code 2017 (With Amendments upto 2020), Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Government of India , 2021, ISBN No. 978-81-936846-0-3

2 .

Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Eco-Niwas Samhita 2018 (Energy Conservation Building Code for Residential Buildings, Part I: Building Envelope), Bureau of Energy Efficiency Government of India , 2018, ISBN No.: 978-81-936846-3-4

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Eco-Niwas Samhita 2021(Code Compliance and Part-II: Electro-Mechanical and Renewable Energy Systems), Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Government of India , 2021
